title: Investigation of the genetic basis of unexplained monogenic diseases
summary:
The study deals with unexplained congenital, genetic diseases in patients. The individual congenital diseases are usually rare (less than 1 patient per 2000 people). The diseases can be very different with the same cause or very similar with different causes. This makes it difficult to clarify the respective cause. In addition, the causative genes are not known for all congenital syndromes or for all patient groups, so that the diagnosis remains unclear for many of those affected.
The genetic material (the “genome”) of every human being consists of a material called DNA (English abbreviation for “deoxyribonucleic acid”) and contains the blueprints (genes) for the structure and function of our body. Errors in genes that lead to congenital diseases are called mutations or pathogenic variants. If you would like to know more about how genes work and different types of mutations, please ask the doctor who gave you the brochure. The study “Investigation of the genetic basis of unexplained monogenic diseases” is a scientific investigation in which we want to uncover and understand such gene mutations as the cause of the respective disease. Monogenic means that the cause of the disease lies in the genetic alteration of only one gene.

interventions.name: (A) Potential participants in this study, i.e. patients with monogenic diseases of unknown genetic cause, will be presented at the Institute of Human Genetics and Genomedicine at RWTH Aachen University for a human genetic consultation.
